offers_products.reason: Sells prescription OUD medicines: Suboxone film, Sublocade (buprenorphine extended-release injection) and related buprenorphine products.

offers_services.reason: Revenue comes from pharmaceutical products; advocacy and education are not paid services.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Patients with OUD receive the prescription medicines, though prescribers and payers influence the choice.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Sells through wholesalers, pharmacies, clinics and government/healthcare systems that buy and dispense Suboxone and Sublocade.

recurring_revenue.reason: Chronic OUD treatment means patients refill Suboxone and receive monthly Sublocade injections on an ongoing basis.

cyclical_demand.reason: Prescription addiction treatment for a chronic disease is medically necessary and not easily postponed in a downturn.

big_ticket.reason: Monthly prescriptions and injections are small, frequent purchases rather than large infrequent ones.

people_delivered.reason: Value is in patented pharmaceutical products, not staff time; a drug maker.

large_customers.reason: Patients are the end users, but direct buyers are large wholesalers, payers and government programs; mixed, leaning consumer-facing.

asset_heavy.reason: Specialty pharma with offices and research centers; manufacturing appears outsourced, so it needs no heavy plants or fleets.

notes: Large_customers is uncertain: wholesalers and payers are large, but the website text names patients as end users.
